newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold down on professional sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold down on professional sales.

text.p: Hong Kong's gold market saw continuous professional selling on Monday on gold's recent disappointing performance, traders and dealers said.
"We saw some disappointed long liquidation from last Friday," said one source at an international bank's bullion house, noting that the market pick-up to $381 had failed to follow through.

"We saw offers to sell at about $380, but below $380 there was some buying interest," said another senior bullion trader, noting that the Asian gold market was much like a wrestling match, with rises countered by falls.
Traders saw gold trading in a $379-380 range in the near term but said that price trends were still southwards.
Volume was said to be thinner than usual with Australian players on holiday.
Japanese traders were heard offering gold in the market, but not at aggressive prices, sources said.
The level of physical demand was said routine for Mondays, boosted by demand from jewellery factories who had depleted supplies over the weekend, gold sources said.
Physical demand would pick up after a few days when supplies bought at the $380-382 level were used up, some traders said.

The involvement of Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp in a $20 billion class action for allegedly not returning money, jewellery and other assets to victims of Nazis had not affected the gold market, traders said, noting that it was too early to tell what the legal outcome would be.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$379.50/380.00 an ounce Monday against New York's US$380.25/75 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$6 lower at HK$3,498 a tael. The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Society remained unchanged from its Friday fix at -5.
